interpretations: "How much each film rating gets rented" is the number of rentals per rating. The average across ratings is the mean of those five counts. The row has two values: the mean rental count of the ratings above that mean, and the average amount by which those ratings exceed the mean

Same as 1, but the "average figure for those ratings" is the mean of their rental counts and the "how far above" is that mean minus the overall average. The result is the same number as the average excess, but it is computed as a single difference
Same as 1, but the overall average is taken over all rentals, as total rentals divided by 5 ratings. This is the same as the mean of the per-rating counts
"How much each rating gets rented" is the number of distinct rented inventory copies per rating, not the number of rental events
"How much each rating gets rented" is the number of distinct films rented per rating
"How much each rating gets rented" is the number of distinct customers renting each rating
"How much each rating gets rented" is the total rental revenue per rating, from payments joined via rental. The path then runs payment to rental to inventory to film
"How much each rating gets rented" is the total rental duration per rating, as days between rental_date and return_date
"How much each rating gets rented" is the average rentals per film within each rating, which is the rental count divided by the number of films in that rating
"How much each rating gets rented" is the average rentals per inventory copy within each rating
The overall average is a weighted average over all rentals, not the mean of the per-rating figures. Ratings above it are then compared against that weighted figure
The ratings are compared with a strictly greater-than test against the overall average. A non-strict version would include ratings equal to it
The join from rental to inventory to film is an inner join. Films or copies that were never rented are excluded, so some ratings may have counts from rented items only
The join is a left join from film or inventory. Unrented copies count as zero rentals, which matters for the per-film and per-copy readings
"How far above the overall average they are on average" is the average of the absolute differences (rating figure minus overall average) across the above-average ratings
"How far above" is a percentage or ratio above the overall average, not an absolute difference
"How far above" is the difference between the mean of the above-average ratings and the overall average of all ratings, as a single difference of two means
The output is one row with two columns, the average figure and the average excess. Alternatively, the one row could be shown with the overall average as an extra column
The values are returned unrounded, as raw decimals
Missing interpretations:
"How much each film rating gets rented" is the number of payment records per rating, reached by going from payment to rental to inventory to film
"How much each film rating gets rented" is the number of rentals per rating counting only returned rentals (return_date is not null)
"How much each film rating gets rented" is the number of rentals per rating counting only unreturned or currently outstanding rentals
"How much each film rating gets rented" is the share or percentage of all rentals that each rating accounts for. The above-average ratings are then those whose share is above 20%
"The average across ratings" is the average over the rating-level figures that include only ratings with at least one rental. This differs from dividing by a fixed 5 if a rating has no rentals
"On average" in "how far above the overall average they are on average" is read as the sum of the excesses, not the mean of the excesses
queries:
WITH rc AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM rental r
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
m AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS mean_cnt FROM rc
)
SELECT AVG(rc.cnt) AS mean_rental_count_above_mean,
       AVG(rc.cnt - m.mean_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_mean
FROM rc, m
WHERE rc.cnt > m.mean_cnt;
WITH rating_counts AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS rental_count
  FROM rental r
  JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
)
SELECT rating, rental_count, (SELECT SUM(rental_count) * 1.0 / 5 FROM rating_counts) AS overall_avg
FROM rating_counts;
SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT r.inventory_id) AS rented_copies
FROM film f
JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
JOIN rental r ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
GROUP BY f.rating;
SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating
SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT r.customer_id) FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating
